find.question: The publisher pursued by postal inspectors in 1904 over a fraudulent investment scheme had earlier written a guide for aspiring entrepreneurs. Which tactic did that guide promote?
find.answer: Making one small operation look like several large firms by inventing extra company names and departments.
distractors: Advertising only in the newspapers with the biggest circulation.
Offering a full refund to anyone who was not satisfied.
Sending travelling salesmen to call on customers at home.

find.question: A still-active order was founded in 1915 by a man who had worked in advertising. A Florida group that later broke away from it circulated a mailer in 1933 — what authority did that mailer invoke?
find.answer: A hidden council of ascended teachers, an idea taken from Theosophy.
distractors: Sacred writings said to have been recovered from an Egyptian tomb.
A charter signed by a European monarch.
A vision received by the group's own founder.

find.question: The playwright who published the first comedy with a pedant in the leading role also showed that pedant's methods of discipline. What did the technique his pupils complain of involve?
find.answer: Beating a boy on the backside while another pupil carried him on his back.
distractors: Making a boy recite Latin aloud for hours on end.
Locking a pupil alone in a dark room.
Making a boy copy out a whole grammar book overnight.

find.question: One schoolmaster character explains that his title means ‘three times really great’. What becomes of him by the end of the play in which he appears?
find.answer: He is tricked, robbed, and then beaten in the same way he had beaten his own pupils.
distractors: He is promoted and put in charge of the whole school.
He dies of shame once his mistakes are exposed.
He leaves the city quietly with his reputation intact.

find.question: One firm takes its name from objects that appear in Tolkien. In a 2025 book, its chief executive and his legal counsel defended the firm's government work on what grounds?
find.answer: That it answers a deep human wish to belong to something like a warrior brotherhood.
distractors: That the work is simply required by contracts the firm had already signed.
That a rival company would take the same contracts if they refused.
That the money earned pays for the firm's non-military research.

find.question: A company rebranded in 2021 using a term borrowed from a 1992 novel. Near its close, the essay argues that novel's political arrangement has now been realised — in what form?
find.answer: The state hollowed out and replaced by corporate enclaves and privately owned digital territory.
distractors: A worldwide ban on private ownership of virtual land.
Governments taking direct ownership of the major technology platforms.
Physical money disappearing in favour of a single digital token.

find.question: The club secretary who obtained the Clayton ground in 1893, after the club was evicted from its first home, held that post across which span?
Supporters opposed to the 2005 takeover founded a breakaway club. From whom did the man behind that takeover buy his controlling stake?
find.answer: Two Irish horse-racing businessmen who had become the club's largest shareholders.
distractors: A group of investors from the Middle East.
The club's former manager and his family.
A satellite television broadcaster.

find.question: The team named their oldest Bosnian pine after a Greek god. To reconstruct past summer temperatures from that tree rather than past drought, which property of the wood did they turn to?
find.answer: The density of the wood, since warm summers let the tree build thicker cell walls.
distractors: The amount of resin sealed into each ring.
The chemistry of the carbon stored in each ring.
The angle at which the cells lean inside each ring.

find.question: One bristlecone pine is named after a famously long-lived biblical figure. How far back does the chronology assembled from bristlecone wood reach, compared with that tree's own first ring?
distractors: About fifty years earlier.
About two hundred years later.
About the same year.

find.question: Two businessmen agreed in 1887 to fund Tesla and manage his patents. What terms did they obtain from Westinghouse the following year?
find.answer: A lump sum in cash and stock, plus a royalty on every unit of motor power sold.
distractors: An outright purchase of the patents, with nothing paid afterwards.
A seat on the Westinghouse board in place of any payment.
Funding for a laboratory in exchange for all of Tesla's future inventions.

find.question: US officials feared Tesla's papers might pass to an exiled Yugoslav politician who was his nephew. What did that man's later pressure bring about?
find.answer: The whole estate was crated up and shipped to Belgrade.
distractors: The papers were sealed by court order for fifty years.
The FBI printed a full list of the seized material in the newspapers.
The estate was sold at public auction to pay off unpaid hotel bills.
